result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both cards have nearly the same structure: comfortable padding, right-aligned prices, a total set apart by a rule and extra space, and a solid button with an understated text link. A groups its content more cleanly, with the title and date close together and a clear gap before the line items. B's tinted date box is cramped in the narrower card, with the date and time pushed close together. Both buttons measure about 50px in the screenshots, just over the 48px limit, and item 4 is scored from what the screenshots show because the CSS wasn't available. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both cards have comfortable outer padding (about 24 px in A, about 28 px in B), right-aligned prices, a rule plus a larger gap before the total, and a low-emphasis Change dates link. In both screenshots the button measures about 51 px tall, a little over the 48 px limit. B wins because its title-to-date gap is clearly smaller than the gaps between sections, while A puts the date and time in a tinted box with cramped insides and a weaker size difference between gaps; the CSS couldn't be read for item 4, so that score is an estimate from the screenshots.
